result.summary: Read core-directives.md and security-invariants.md (all S1-S14) in full, docs/agents/design/REQ-026.md in full, then the actual diff myself (git diff master...HEAD) rather than trusting BACKEND-DEV's or REVIEWER's characterizations: domain/notification.ts (full diff), scheduler/rateLimiter.ts (full diff), domain/registration.ts's new reconfirm block (full), handlers/reminder24h.ts (full, new file), scheduler/reminderJobs.ts (full, new file), domain/reminders.ts (full, new file), domain/event.ts's findDoorsAgendaItem addition, handlers/withdraw.ts's export/wrapper diff, index.ts's sequencing diff, i18n diffs. S9/S10 EXTENSION CHECK (task item 3): traced sendLedgeredNotification's step 5 myself rather than trusting REVIEWER's 'pure wrapper migration' characterization. Steps 1-4 (user lookup, blocked check, marketing broadcastOptIn check, atomic ledger INSERT keyed (registrationId,kind)) are byte-for-byte unchanged from REQ-025. Step 5 now: composeMessage is called ONLY after step 4's insert has already committed (same position in the function body, confirmed by reading the diff hunk directly -- no reordering); a {kind:'skip'} result returns {kind:'skipped-stale'} with NO sender call made (grepped the diff -- the composed-kind branch that returns early never touches input.sender); {kind:'text'}/{kind:'photo'} call the matching sender method; either call's success/throw still maps to sent/failed exactly as before. The whole composeMessage-and-send sequence remains inside the same try/catch as REQ-025's, so sendLedgeredNotification still never throws (composeMessage errors are caught here too, not propagated to the job runner). This confirms REVIEWER's characterization was correct, independently re-derived rather than copied. NEW AUTHORIZATION SURFACE -- reminder24h:confirm/:decline forgery (task item 4, PRIMARY FOCUS): constructed my own adversarial scenario distinct from REVIEWER's scope (REVIEWER did not test this). Wrote and ran three own DB-backed adversarial tests (scratch file apps/bot/src/handlers/_sec_adversarial.test.ts, written, run against the real scratch Postgres at localhost:55432, then deleted -- not committed, confirmed via git status --short clean afterward): (1) Attacker with NO registration of their own sends `reminder24h:confirm:` naming a real victim's admitted registration -> handler resolves actingUser from the ATTACKER's own tgId (resolveActingUser(db, BigInt(attackerTgId))), then decideReconfirmOutcome compares ownerUserId (victim's user id, read fresh via SELECT...FOR UPDATE inside reconfirmRegistration's own transaction) against actingUserId (attacker's) -> mismatch -> {kind:'not-owner'} -> handler replies catalog.withdraw.refusedNotFound (non-disclosure). Verified: victim's reconfirmed_at stayed NULL, admission stayed 'admitted', zero registration.reconfirm audit rows for the victim's registration id. (2) Same attacker sends `reminder24h:decline:` -> withdrawRegistration's own decideWithdrawOutcome performs the identical ownerUserId check (traced in registration.ts lines ~456-477, pre-existing REQ-022/023 code, unchanged by this diff) -> {kind:'not-owner'} -> refusedNotFound reply. Verified: victim's admission stayed 'admitted' (seat NOT freed), zero registration.withdraw audit rows for the victim's id. (3) Attacker who DOES have their own separate admitted registration to the same event forges a decline naming the VICTIM's registration id instead of their own -> same not-owner rejection; victim's row untouched, attacker's own registration also untouched (the handler never substitutes the acting user's own registration when the named id doesn't belong to them -- it refuses outright rather than silently redirecting). All 3 tests passed on a real run (`TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run apps/bot/src/handlers/_sec_adversarial.test.ts --no-file-parallelism` -> 3 passed). CONCLUSION: a forged reminder24h callback naming another user's registration id CANNOT reconfirm or withdraw on their behalf -- both reconfirmRegistration and withdrawRegistration re-derive ownership from a fresh, transaction-locked DB read of the registration row and compare it against the CALLER's own resolved identity (from ctx.from.id, not from the callback_data payload), matching the discipline REQ-022's /withdraw confirm callback already established. This is genuine defense-in-depth: even though Telegram callback_data is not attacker-forgeable through the normal client (a callback_query is only generated by tapping a button on a message actually delivered to that chat), the code does not rely on that assumption -- it checks ownership server-side regardless of what the callback_data claims. 'CAN'T MAKE IT' REUSE (task item 5): confirmed handlers/reminder24h.ts's decline handler calls `withdrawRegistration(db, registrationId, actingUser.id, new Date())` directly, imported unchanged from domain/registration.ts -- zero lines of registration.ts's existing withdraw logic were touched by this diff (git diff shows only ADDITIONS after the existing withdrawRegistration function, not modifications to it). The promotion side-effect (`sendPromotionNotification`, exported by this diff by adding one `export` keyword and changing only its composeMessage closure's return-value WRAPPER (bare string -> {kind:'text', text}, same string) is called identically to withdraw.ts's own confirm handler. This is the same already-audited path, not a parallel/weaker implementation -- confirmed by reading withdraw.ts's diff hunk directly (7 lines changed total, all wrapper-shape). AT-SEND-TIME RE-CHECK (task item 6, AC4): traced structurally, not just by reading the design doc's claim. selectRegistrationsForReminder24h/3h (domain/reminders.ts) return only {registrationId, userId} -- no admission/status data is carried forward from the selection query. Each candidate is then passed to sendLedgeredNotification, whose composeMessage closure (reminderJobs.ts's composeReminder24h/composeReminder3h) calls `getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent(db, registrationId)` -- a BRAND NEW SELECT issued at the moment step 5 runs (i.e. after the ledger insert, immediately before send), structurally incapable of reusing stale data from the selection query because the selection query's result type doesn't even carry an admission field to reuse. If admission !== 'admitted' at that fresh read, {kind:'skip'} is returned and skipped-stale is recorded with no send. This genuinely re-reads live state at send time, not a stale snapshot -- confirmed by the absence of any admission/status field on ReminderCandidate (domain/reminders.ts's own interface) that could even be threaded through if someone tried. NEW PII EXPOSURE (task item 7): the T-3h message/QR exposes event title, chapter-timezone start/doors time, venue address, both map links, and a QR encoding `https://t.me/?start=ci_` (confirmed by reading domain/qr.ts directly -- renderCheckInQrPng's deep-link template is UNCHANGED, byte-identical to REQ-024's). Every one of these fields is already shown to the same registrant via /my (handlers/my.ts calls the identical renderCheckInQrPng with the identical qrToken read from the same registrations row). No other user's data is read or sent by either job -- selectRegistrationsForReminder24h/3h scope every send to that registration's own userId (candidate.userId, used as sendLedgeredNotification's userId, which resolves that same user's own tgId to send to). No cross-user leak. INDEX.TS SEQUENCING FIX (task item 8): read the diff directly. `await bot.init()` now precedes both `startScheduledJobs([...])` and the read of `bot.botInfo.username` -- confirmed by line order in the diff hunk (init await, then const botUsername = bot.botInfo.username, then startScheduledJobs(...), then bot.start() unchanged as the file's last call). bot.init() is the grammY call that performs the getMe request populating botInfo; since it is awaited before startScheduledJobs is ever called, no job's first (immediate, per runner.ts's 'immediate first run' rule) execution can occur before botInfo exists. No window found where a job could fire with an uninitialized bot. COMMANDS RUN BY ME, REAL OUTPUT: `npm run lint` (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors, 2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings, unrelated to this diff. `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces clean (Next.js + bot tsc). `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root) -> 22 files / 249 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. My own 3 adversarial ownership tests (scratch file, not committed) -> 3/3 passed on a real run against the same scratch Postgres. S13 MIGRATION SIGN-OFF: `git diff --name-only master...HEAD` contains zero files under apps/bot/drizzle/ -- no migration of any kind ships with this diff, matching the design doc's header claim ('Schema change: NO') and REQ-011's registrations.reconfirmed_at column (already existed, REQ-026 is merely its first writer) and NotificationKind's two new union members (a TypeScript-only change against the already-text `kind` column REQ-025 shipped). S13's mandatory sign-off trigger (a migration dropping/renaming/rewriting a personal-data or attendance column) is not met -- confirmed by absence, not by trusting the design doc's own claim. Remaining S1-S14 items, each re-derived against this diff specifically: - S1 (consent precedes storage): N/A -- no User/Profile consent-column writes anywhere in this diff; confirmed by reading every new/changed file (registration.ts's reconfirm block, reminders.ts, reminderJobs.ts, reminder24h.ts) for any write to consent_pd_at/broadcast_opt_in/publish_consent -- none exists; broadcastOptIn is read-only (unchanged from REQ-025). - S2: PASS, see primary-focus section above -- own adversarial negative case constructed and run for both confirm and decline callbacks, both correctly refuse an unauthorized actor and neither writes a state change nor an audit row for the unauthorized attempt. - S3 (member reads only own Profile): N/A for new reads -- getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent and the reminder selection queries are both scoped to one registrationId/userId at a time, driven server-side by the selection query and the callback's own resolved actingUser, never by a cross-user list; no new list/search/export surface introduced. - S4 (tokens unguessable): N/A -- no token generation in this diff; the T-3h path reads the registration's own pre-existing qr_token (REQ-020, unchanged), read-only. - S5/S6/S7 (check-in refusal/audit, checked_in_at gating, capacity+override audit): N/A -- no check-in or capacity code touched; confirmed handlers/checkin.ts absent from `git diff --name-only master...HEAD`; reconfirmRegistration's UPDATE touches only reconfirmed_at (confirmed by reading its one UPDATE statement -- admission is never in the SET clause), so AC2's 'admission unchanged' holds structurally, and S6/S7 are untouched by construction. - S8 (exactly one AuditLog row per status change): PASS -- reconfirmRegistration writes exactly one writeAuditLog call (action: registration.reconfirm) inside the same transaction as its one UPDATE, only on the 'reconfirmed' branch (every other outcome returns before reaching the write, confirmed by reading the early-return guard). The decline path reuses withdrawRegistration unchanged, already S8-audited under REQ-022/023. - S9: PASS -- see extension-check section above; ledger insert (steps 1-4) genuinely unchanged, still the sole serialization point; composeMessage's new skip/text/photo branches all sit strictly after it. - S10: PASS -- both jobs call sendLedgeredNotification with classification:'transactional' (confirmed by reading reminderJobs.ts's two call sites directly), so REQ-025's step 3 broadcastOptIn check is skipped entirely for both -- AC10 holds structurally, not by testing luck. - S11 (PII never in plaintext logs): checked runner.ts's log.error('scheduled job failed', {job: job.name, error: err}) call, now reachable for the first time (REQ-025 flagged this as a forward-looking MINOR risk once real jobs shipped). Traced whether either job's run() can throw an error containing PII: selectRegistrationsForReminder24h/3h could throw a raw DB error (connectivity/query-shape, not per-user PII); every per-candidate call goes through sendLedgeredNotification, which (confirmed above) still never throws -- composeMessage errors are caught inside sendLedgeredNotification's own try/catch and returned as {kind:'failed'}, never propagated to the job's for-loop or the runner's catch. So the only error that can reach runner.ts's log.error from these two jobs is a DB-level query failure, not a per-message/per-user payload -- REQ-025's forward-looking S11 concern does not materialize in this diff. No new console./log. call was added anywhere in the new reminder code (grepped domain/reminders.ts, scheduler/reminderJobs.ts, handlers/reminder24h.ts, domain/registration.ts's new block -- zero matches). - S12 (exports role-gated/audited): N/A -- no export functionality in this diff. - S13: PASS -- see migration sign-off above; zero migration files, sign-off trigger not met. - S14 (publication consent default-off): N/A -- no Profile/publish_consent code touched. Also closed out REQ-025's own forward-looking MINOR ('future sendLedgeredNotification callers must supply only server-derived ids'): confirmed both reminderJobs.ts call sites pass registrationId/userId taken directly from selectRegistrationsForReminder24h/3h's own DB query rows (ReminderCandidate), never from Telegram update data -- the guidance was followed. Scope/hygiene check: `git status --short` clean after my own scratch adversarial test file was deleted; no stray file left in the working tree beyond this handoff and the JSON I am about to commit. Verdict: PASS. Both the S9/S10 extension and this requirement's new authorization surface (reminder24h confirm/decline callbacks) hold under my own independently-constructed adversarial cases, not merely REVIEWER's positive-path verification. No blocking defect found across S1-S14.

evidence.forged_callback_result: CANNOT act on another user's registration. Both reconfirmRegistration and withdrawRegistration re-derive ownership from a fresh, row-locked DB read of the registration (never from callback_data or any reminder-message-time snapshot) and compare it against the caller's own identity resolved from ctx.from.id via resolveActingUser -- a mismatch returns not-owner/not-found (non-disclosing) with no write and no audit row, for both an attacker with no registration of their own and an attacker who owns a different registration to the same event. Verified with 3 own DB-backed adversarial tests, all passing.
evidence.s9_extension_check: sendLedgeredNotification's ledger-insert-then-send ordering (REQ-025 steps 1-4) is untouched; the new skip/text/photo branching (step 5) sits strictly after the committed insert and never causes a sender call on skip. Confirmed by direct diff read, not by trusting REVIEWER's characterization.
evidence.at_send_time_recheck: Confirmed structurally impossible to reuse a stale snapshot: ReminderCandidate (selection-time) carries no admission/status field at all, forcing composeMessage to issue a brand-new getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent SELECT at send time.
